topIssues.title: kona-tests: TestConnDropSync flakes when the sequencer still lists the disconnected validator
topIssues.author: aakoshh
topIssues.body:
`TestConnDropSync` in `rust/kona/tests/node/restart` can fail right after it disconnects the validator from the sequencer, because it checks the sequencer's peer list before the sequencer has noticed the disconnection.

### Failure
[`rust-e2e-restart` on #23874](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5822627), on a commit that only changed a comment in an unrelated Rust test:

```
conn_drop_test.go:44: node cl-reth-kona-validator-0 is disconnected from sequencer cl-reth-kona-sequencer-0
Error Trace: rust/kona/tests/node/restart/conn_drop_test.go:47
Messages:    expected node cl-reth-kona-validator-0 to be disconnected from sequencer cl-reth-kona-sequencer-0
--- FAIL: TestConnDropSync (20.02s)
```

The same job passed on the branch's previous run, and `rust-e2e-restart` passed 509 of its last 509 runs on `develop`, so it's rare.

### Cause
- `L2CLNode.DisconnectPeer` (`op-devstack/dsl/l2_cl.go:630`) only calls the validator's `opp2p_disconnectPeer`. That returns once the validator has closed its side of the connection.
- The test then reads `sequencer.Peers()` once and requires the validator to be gone (`conn_drop_test.go:44-47`).
- The sequencer drops the connection only when the close reaches it, so the read can come first. In the failing run, the disconnect log and the failed assertion share a millisecond (`15:56:43.048`).

The validator-side check right after it (`node.Peers()`) can't race this way, since `opp2p_disconnectPeer` waits for the validator's own state.

### Fix
Retry the sequencer-side check until the validator is gone, with a timeout, as the test already does for the sync checks below it (`wait.For`). Or make `DisconnectPeer` wait until both sides have dropped the connection, so that every caller gets that guarantee.

topIssues.title: op-interop-filter: Retry ingestion when the EL RPC is down at start-up
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
If a chain's EL RPC is down when ingestion starts, the ingester exits and never retries. It sets no error and `up` stays 1, but every check fails as not ready. Interop then stops on all chains until someone restarts the filter.

Retry ingestion start-up, or exit the process when it fails, so that the failure is visible and recovers.

Blocks launch.

Filed by Claude from the Lagoon interop FMA (FM23).

topIssues.title: op-interop-filter: Keep the manual failsafe across restarts
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
`admin_setFailsafeEnabled(true)` sets a flag in memory only. A restart (deploy, out-of-memory, reschedule) clears it. After backfill, the filter approves messages again, with no operator action, during an incident that the operator meant to hold.

Store the manual failsafe in the data directory, or add a start flag that turns it on.

Does not block launch.

Filed by Claude from the Lagoon interop FMA (FM22).

topIssues.title: op-interop-filter: Check that the backfill duration covers the expiry window
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
If `--backfill-duration` is shorter than the message expiry window, the filter returns `SkippedData` for an initiating message older than the backfill. op-reth then evicts a valid transaction. The default (168 h) matches the window, but the configuration does not enforce this.

Add a configuration check that rejects a backfill duration shorter than the expiry window.

Does not block launch.

Filed by Claude from the Lagoon interop FMA (FM20).

topIssues.title: op-interop-filter: Take the chain set from the dependency set
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
op-interop-filter takes its chain set from its `--l2-rpcs` entries, not from the dependency set. An extra `--l2-rpcs` entry makes a chain outside the dependency set a valid source. The filter then approves executing messages that op-supernode invalidates, and each invalid message causes a reorg.

Make the filter read the dependency set. It must reject an RPC for a chain that is not in the dependency set.

Does not block launch.

Filed by Claude from the Lagoon interop FMA (FM19).

topPRs.title: op-acceptance-tests,op-devstack: cover eth version negotiation and transaction propagation between op-reth and op-geth
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Nothing checked how op-reth and op-geth peer and exchange transactions: `rust/op-reth/crates/node/tests/it/p2p_version.rs` pins the version two op-reth nodes negotiate, and every devstack peering is trusted, which exempts the session from the reputation handling the reth 2.6 bump (#23046) changes along with the default protocol (eth/71) and the transaction fetcher (reth#26924, a per-peer cap of 4096 announced hashes). This adds an acceptance test package that peers an op-reth follower and an op-geth follower as basic peers and checks the negotiated version, transaction propagation in both directions, and op-reth under an announcement burst from op-geth, written against hooks that are the same on `develop` and on the bump.

## What the tests cover

All three tests run on a `pairSystem` (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_opgeth_peering/system_test.go`): an op-reth sequencer, an op-reth follower and an op-geth follower, 1s blocks. One follower is the *sender*: it is kept off the mixed runtime's trusted mesh (`IsolateFromL2P2P`), its consensus client is peered with the sequencer's alone, and it dials the other follower (the *receiver*) with the new `PeerWithBasic`, so the receiver is its only execution-layer peer and the session is trusted on neither side. The receiver keeps the trusted peering with the sequencer that the runtime set up. A transaction submitted to the sender can therefore only reach the sequencer through the receiver, so its inclusion proves it crossed the peering under test; with the sequencer paused, the receiver's pool can be observed. The system is returned once the sender has filled its gap to the chain through the receiver.

- `TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion`, subtests `op-reth_dials_op-geth` and `op-geth_dials_op-reth`: both sides must report the same negotiated eth version through `admin_peers`, equal to the highest version both advertise (`sysgo.HighestCommonEthVersion` over the two `caps` lists), and the advertised versions are logged.
- `TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock`, subtests `op-reth_to_op-geth` and `op-geth_to_op-reth`: with the sequencer paused, a transfer submitted to the sender must show up in the receiver's pool (`eth_getTransactionByHash` with no block), and once the sequencer resumes both followers must see it in the same block.
- `TestOpRethKeepsItsOpGethPeerThroughAnAnnouncementBurst`: op-geth is the sender. 4112 fresh accounts (the cap plus one fan-out of 16) each submit one transaction with 4096 bytes of zero calldata to op-geth in batch calls while the sequencer is paused. op-geth sends a transaction larger than its `txMaxBroadcastSize` (4096 bytes) to no peer whole: it announces the hash (`eth/handler.go`, `BroadcastTransactions`), so the burst is 4112 `NewPooledTransactionHashes` entries to op-reth within about a second, which op-reth has to fetch. The test requires op-reth's pool to reach at least 4096 of them, op-reth to keep the same session with op-geth (same remote port in `admin_peers`; a drop followed by op-geth's static re-dial would show a new one) and to log nothing at error level, and once the sequencer resumes, op-reth's pool to drain down to at most 16 and its head to keep advancing. How many of the burst op-reth fetched and how many each follower still holds afterwards are logged.

What the burst can and cannot show: the number of hashes announced exceeds what op-reth tracks per peer after the bump, but op-reth fetches while the burst is still arriving, and whether its unfetched set from op-geth ever reached 4096 (the point where it drops further announcements) is not observable through RPC. The test therefore proves that op-reth takes a cap-sized announcement burst from an untrusted op-geth peer in its stride, not that the drop path ran. Proving the latter needs reth's `announced_hashes_dropped_peer_limit` metric, which the mixed runtime does not expose. The drain bound of 16 rather than 0 is for the same cap downstream: op-reth passes the burst to the sequencer, which fetches what op-reth only announced to it, so a cap-sized fetch there can strand up to one fan-out in op-reth's pool; every run below drained to 0.

Each sender has exactly one transaction, so a hash the fetcher drops cannot leave a nonce gap behind; the accounts are funded through a tree of distributors (`funding_test.go`) because reth holds at most 16 transactions per account (`--txpool.max-account-slots`, and the runtime passes `--txpool.nolocals`), which also bounds every funding round to one batch per payer.

Matrix: direction {op-reth to op-geth, op-geth to op-reth} as subtests (the dialing side is the sender, so both dial directions are covered too); CL {op-node, kona-node} through `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND`. Skips on `DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth` (the sequencer is this tree's op-reth).

## Local verification

Debug op-reth built from this stack's Rust tree (identical to `develop`'s), kona-node release binary from `develop`'s `rust/kona`, `-parallel 2`, under `caffeinate`:

```
cd <worktree> && DEVSTACK_ORCHESTRATOR=sysgo RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_RETH=<op-reth> RUST_BINARY_PATH_KONA_NODE=<kona-node> \
  go test -count=1 -timeout 40m -parallel 2 -run 'TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion|TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock|TestOpRethKeepsItsOpGethPeerThroughAnAnnouncementBurst' -v ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_opgeth_peering/
```

`develop` op-reth, op-node (default): all five cells pass, 69s for the package.

```
--- PASS: TestOpRethKeepsItsOpGethPeerThroughAnAnnouncementBurst (37.56s)
--- PASS: TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock/op-reth_to_op-geth (23.08s)
--- PASS: TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock/op-geth_to_op-reth (23.02s)
--- PASS: TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion/op-reth_dials_op-geth (20.54s)
--- PASS: TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion/op-geth_dials_op-reth (21.94s)
```

`develop` op-reth, `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node`: all five cells pass, 100s.

```
--- PASS: TestOpRethKeepsItsOpGethPeerThroughAnAnnouncementBurst (46.95s)
--- PASS: TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock/op-reth_to_op-geth (36.33s)
--- PASS: TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock/op-geth_to_op-reth (33.36s)
--- PASS: TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion/op-reth_dials_op-geth (31.98s)
--- PASS: TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion/op-geth_dials_op-reth (29.74s)
```

Against #23046's op-reth (reth 2.6.0, built from the bump head 93d9ec9d2f, op-node): all five cells pass, 71s.

```
--- PASS: TestOpRethKeepsItsOpGethPeerThroughAnAnnouncementBurst (36.82s)
--- PASS: TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock/op-reth_to_op-geth (22.28s)
--- PASS: TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock/op-geth_to_op-reth (28.46s)
--- PASS: TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion/op-reth_dials_op-geth (23.69s)
--- PASS: TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion/op-geth_dials_op-reth (19.67s)
```

Negotiated versions, as the verification criterion asks: op-geth v1.101702.4-rc.1 advertises `eth/69` only (`eth/protocols/eth/protocol.go`, `ProtocolVersions = {ETH69}`). `develop`'s op-reth advertises `eth/66` to `eth/69`, the bump's `eth/66` to `eth/71`; the pair negotiates **eth/69** on both, in both dial directions, so on the bump op-reth falls back two versions from its own eth/71 to op-geth's highest. The peering is untrusted on both sides (asserted inside `PeerWithBasic`); op-reth marks op-geth's entry static when op-reth dials, op-geth marks op-reth's static when op-geth dials.

Burst: op-reth's pool held 4107 to 4112 of the 4112 at the first poll after the batches were accepted, on `develop` and on the bump alike (4105 to 4112 across all runs), the session kept its remote port and eth/69, no op-reth error log, and after the sequencer resumed every burst transaction was included within 6s: 0 left in op-reth and 0 left in op-geth in every run.

Unit: `go test ./op-service/txplan/ ./op-devstack/sysgo/ -run 'TestHighest|TestPeerInfo|TestPeerIDMatches|TestPollPeerList|TestPinnedFields'` and `go test -run TestFunding ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_opgeth_peering/` pass; `linter/bin/op-golangci-lint run` on the changed packages reports no issue.

## Observations

- An isolated op-geth follower under op-node logs `Failed to get payload ... err="Unsupported fork"` while it is behind the chain: op-node derives attributes from L1 and asks op-geth to seal them, which op-geth refuses under the devnet's Karst-at-genesis config. The follower catches up through the receiver instead, and the same lines appear on `develop`; noted, not investigated.
- On this machine, under two concurrent devnets, an op-geth follower that is both gap-filling and peered with two consensus clients once answered its user RPC with `dial tcp 127.0.0.1:<port>: i/o timeout` for 30s. The pair keeps the sender's consensus client on a single peer (the sequencer's), which never showed it in nine runs since.

## Seams

- `sysgo.ConnectP2PBasic` / `dsl.L2ELNode.PeerWithBasic`: a basic peering (static entry on the dialer, nothing on the acceptor, trusted on neither side, asserted after connecting). `PeerWith` stays trusted on both sides; `DisconnectPeerWith` undoes `PeerWith` only.
- `dsl.L2ELNode.VerifyPeeredWith`, `PeerInfoOf`, `Peers` over `sysgo.PeerInfo` / `ListPeers` / `ELPeerInfo` (caps, negotiated eth version or 0 during the handshake, inbound/static/trusted, session addresses), `sysgo.HighestEthVersion` and `HighestCommonEthVersion`.
- `dsl.L2ELNode.SendTransactions` (batched `eth_sendRawTransaction`), `WaitForPooledTransaction`, `TxPoolStatus`, `TxPoolReached`, `TxPoolHoldsAtMost`, `TxPoolDrained`.
- `dsl.EOA.PlanOffline`, `Sign`, `Submit`; `txplan.WithStaticChainID`. `txplan.WithGasFeeCap` now drops the default fee-cap computation the way `WithGasLimit` drops the estimator, so a pinned fee cap stays pinned when the tip cap is pinned after it or a block is fetched (it was silently recomputed from the tip cap and the base fee); the one existing caller, `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/loadtest/l2.go`, now gets the 10,000 gwei cap it asked for, which its budget already accounts for.

`go-code-reviewer` was run and every finding addressed: the `bigint` lint, the burst's claim re-scoped as above and its drain bound, both followers gated on the funding blocks before the burst and the transfer, the expected version as the highest common one rather than the smaller maximum, `Peers` listing handshaking peers too, the session check guarded to the accepting side, per-poll logging in the pool waits, and the setup re-checks, unused `Fn` variant, duplicated node-info lookups and inaccurate comments removed.

Stacked on #23440, #23438, #23436, #23431, #23427, #23421 and #23418.

Closes #23402

topPRs.title: op-acceptance-tests,op-devstack: cover forkchoice updates with a stale safe or finalized hash
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
reth 2.6 (#23046) carries reth#27247 and reth#27429: a forkchoice update whose safe or finalized hash is not on the head's chain is refused with `-38002` before anything is applied, and a persisted header is canonical only when it matches the canonical hash at its height. On `develop` the green acceptance suites only touch these paths incidentally. This adds the four scenarios of #23399 as acceptance tests, written for the bump's documented behavior, with the cells `develop`'s reth 2.5.2 answers differently skipped naming #23046 and the observed answer quoted.

## What the tests cover

All in `op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_stale_forkchoice`, on the mixed runtime at a 1s block time with an op-reth sequencer and an op-reth follower, both without proofs history and both with `--engine.persistence-threshold` and `--engine.memory-block-buffer-target=5` explicit. The follower's consensus client runs the cell's sync mode (`sysgo.L2CLVerifierSyncMode`, from #23421); kona-node has no CL sync mode, so its `cl_sync` cells skip with that reason, as in #23421.

1. `TestFollowerSafeHeadAdvancesAgainAfterL1ReorgRewindsIt` (`cl_sync`, `el_sync`): with the test sequencer building L1 one block at a time (`dsl.TestSequencer.SequenceBlocksUntil`, new, the mechanics of `sync/elsync/reorg` as a DSL wait), waits until the follower's safe head derives from an L1 block past the takeover, reorgs that L1 block out from under it while the follower's consensus client keeps running, and requires the follower to replace the safe block that derived from it (`ReorgTriggered`), to have a safe head deriving from the replacing L1 block (`WaitL1OriginHash`), to be safe five blocks past the pre-reorg safe height again, and to be in sync with the sequencer at the safe and unsafe heads.
2. `TestFollowerResyncsFromScratchUnderConsensusClientThatKeptItsHeads` (`cl_sync`, `el_sync`): waits for the follower to finalize a block above genesis, stops its op-reth, wipes its datadir (`dsl.L2ELNode.WipeDatadir`, new) and starts it again while its consensus client keeps running, so the first forkchoice updates the empty node receives name a head, a safe block and a finalized block it has not downloaded, re-peers it with the sequencer and requires it to hold the sequencer's unsafe head and to be safe and finalized at least where it was before the wipe, with its consensus client in sync with the sequencer's at the safe head. Under kona-node the cell skips before the finalized requirement; see CI follow-up.
3. `TestForkchoiceUpdateNamingReorgedOutFinalizedIsRejected` (`head_already_canonical`, `head_reorgs_to_sibling`): stops the batcher, lets the follower get one block past the sequencer's head at that moment (so the safe head stays below the block it replaces, which both tests assert), stops the follower's consensus client, builds a sibling of the follower's head through the engine API (`dsl.L2ELNode.BuildSiblingBlock`, new), inserts it, and sends a forkchoice update that names the replaced head as finalized: in the first cell after the sibling has been made the head, in the second as the update that would make it the head. Requires the engine API's `-38002` error with its `Invalid forkchoice state` message (`ForkchoiceUpdateResult.IsInvalidForkchoiceState`, new) and the head, safe and finalized labels unchanged.
4. `TestForkchoiceUpdateToPersistedReorgedOutHeadIsAppliedWhenReportedValid` (`threshold_7`, `threshold_50`): stops the batcher, lets the follower get `threshold + 5 + 3` blocks past the sequencer's head at that moment (so nothing the batcher had loaded reaches the block it replaces), stops its consensus client, builds a sibling of the block `threshold + 5 + 2` below the head (persisted and dropped from reth's memory on either schedule), reorgs to it, so every replaced block is on disk until reth's disk reorg removes it, and sends a forkchoice update back to the replaced block. The replaced block is not canonical, so the engine must not take it for the head it already has: the answer must be `VALID` with the head already moved back, or `SYNCING`, which makes the replaced block a sync target the follower downloads from the sequencer; either way the follower must end on the replaced block (`ReorgExact`).

Matrix: sync mode {CL, EL} for 1 and 2, threshold {7, 50} for 4, CL {op-node, kona-node} through `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND` (CI runs both). Tests 3 and 4 stop the consensus client before the raw updates, so the sync mode does not reach them. Every test skips on `DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth`.

  go test -count=1 -timeout 40m -parallel 2 -run 'TestForkchoiceUpdate' -v ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_stale_forkchoice/
# then the same with -run 'TestFollower'
```

Unit tests (`go test -run 'Sibling' ./op-devstack/dsl/`, `go test -run 'OpReth' ./op-devstack/sysgo/`): ok. `go vet`, the custom golangci lint on `op-devstack/...` and the new package, and semgrep on the changed files: clean.

## Skipped cells

- `TestForkchoiceUpdateNamingReorgedOutFinalizedIsRejected/head_reorgs_to_sibling` and both `TestForkchoiceUpdateToPersistedReorgedOutHeadIsAppliedWhenReportedValid` cells: fail on `develop` for the reasons quoted in their skip messages; skipped naming #23046, where they must be re-enabled (both pass against the bump under both consensus clients).
- `TestFollowerSafeHeadAdvancesAgainAfterL1ReorgRewindsIt` under kona-node: skipped naming #18676 (see Findings).
- `TestFollowerResyncsFromScratchUnderConsensusClientThatKeptItsHeads/el_sync` under kona-node: resyncs to the unsafe and safe heads, then skips the finalized requirement naming #23399 (see CI follow-up; the kona-node defect needs its own issue, which the skip should then name).
- `cl_sync` cells under kona-node: kona-node has no CL sync mode (as in #23421).
- Everything skips on `DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth`.

## Findings

- `develop` (reth 2.5.2) applies a reorg before it checks the finalized hash: in `head_reorgs_to_sibling` the update naming the replaced head as finalized is refused with `-38002 Invalid forkchoice state`, but the head has moved to the sibling (`a refused forkchoice update must leave the head, safe and finalized blocks as they were: Not equal: expected head 8f37be…9f697c:13, actual 0db6cc…2c2a2a:13`). This is what reth#27247 fixes; the cell is skipped naming #23046.
- `develop` takes a persisted, reorged-out block for canonical as long as it is still on disk: in both `threshold_7` and `threshold_50` the update back to the replaced block is answered `VALID` with the replaced block as `latestValidHash` while the follower's head stays on the sibling (`status=VALID latest_valid_hash=8f9698…014777 head=42103d…200c51:1` at threshold 7, `status=VALID latest_valid_hash=07774d…0a8473 head=aa0354…d2d950:2` at threshold 50), deterministic in three runs. This is reth#27429's case; the test is skipped naming #23046.
- Against #23046's op-reth the same update is answered `VALID` with the head moved back to the replaced block in the same call (reth logs the sibling committed, then the replaced block committed again): the deep reorg loads the replaced blocks back into reth's tree state, so `find_canonical_header` no longer takes the disk copy for canonical and `on_new_head` reorgs back, as reth#27429 describes. The issue's "pinning that it is not reported as valid" assumed the answer would be `SYNCING`; the test pins what both honest answers share, that a `VALID` answer moves the head and a `SYNCING` answer is followed by the sync-back, which `develop` fails and the bump passes.
- With the sibling already the head, `develop` refuses the stale finalized hash correctly (`head_already_canonical` passes): the finalized check happens before the safe check and nothing has been applied yet, so the rule itself is in place and only its ordering relative to the head change is wrong.
- The L1 reorg under a running follower produces no forkchoice rejection on `develop` in either sync mode: op-node logs `L1 head signal indicates a possible L1 re-org`, resets with `reset: detected L1 reorg`, and its subsequent updates move the safe hash back below the unsafe chain the engine still holds, which reth accepts; the follower replaces its safe block and is in sync with the sequencer again within the bounds. reth logs `Changeset cache MISS in range, falling back to aggregate DB-based computation` (WARN) while it recomputes state for the reorg; expected.
- The empty datadir under a running consensus client causes no forkchoice rejection on `develop` either: reth answers the first update, whose head, safe and finalized hashes it has not downloaded, with `SYNCING` (it downloads the safe block first, then the head), op-node logs `temp: cannot prepare unsafe chain for new payload: ... err: updated forkchoice, but node is syncing` and then resets with `expected engine was synced and had unsafe block to reconcile, but cannot find the block: not found`, re-reads its heads from the empty engine and syncs the gap (through its peers in CL sync, through the engine in EL sync); the follower was back on the sequencer's head about six seconds after the wipe in both modes, with safe and finalized back at their pre-wipe heights. In `el_sync` the finalized label only returns once L1 finality catches up again, since op-node's post-EL-sync shortcut (finalized = the EL-sync tip) does not apply to a reset.

- Under kona-node on `develop`, the L1 reorg is not survived: the kona-node sequencer resets its derivation (`Derivation pipeline is being reset: L1 reorg detected`) but keeps building on the unsafe chain whose L1 origin was reorged out (its op-reth commits blocks 42, 43, … on the same chain after the reset), so nothing replaces that chain, every node rejects the old batches (`batch is for different L1 chain, epoch hash does not match l1_block_number=4`) and buffers the rest (`received out-of-order batch for future processing`), and the follower's safe block is never replaced (`operation failed permanently after 90 attempts: expected head to reorg 0x3f26…d122:20, but got 0x3f26…d122:20`). The L1-reorg test skips on kona-node naming #18676 (kona: check L2 reorg due to L1 reorg), the same reason the `sync/elsync/reorg` tests skip there (#22275). A kona-node follower under an op-node sequencer is not covered by this matrix.
- `dsl.L2ELNode.WaitL1OriginHash` looked blocks up with the one-shot, test-failing lookups inside its retry loop; against the bump the follower's `safe` label answered `not found` for a moment right after the L2 reorg and the wait failed the test instead of retrying. The wait now uses the non-fatal lookups like the other pollers (`blockRefByNumber` is new, next to `blockRefByLabel`).
- Under kona-node the follower is not reliably finalized again after the wipe, and in CI its kona-node exited on `Finalize(BlockNotSafe)`; see CI follow-up.

## Seams added

- `stack.DatadirWipeable` with `sysgo.OpReth.WipeDatadir` (op-devstack/sysgo/l2_el_opreth.go), forwarded by the preset EL frontend like `SwitchBinary`, and `dsl.L2ELNode.WipeDatadir`: empties the datadir and, when enabled, the proofs store, and runs `op-reth init` (and `proofs init`) again, so the next `Start` runs the same binary and arguments on an empty chain. The node must be stopped; its p2p key, logs and genesis live outside the datadir, so its identity survives. The two `init` invocations the mixed runtime made inline are now `initOpRethDatadir` and `initOpRethProofsStore`, run under the test context and reporting their output on failure.
- `dsl.L2ELNode.GetPayload(info)`: `engine_getPayload` for the job a forkchoice update with attributes started.
- `dsl.L2ELNode.BuildSiblingBlock(number)`: has the engine build a block that can replace the canonical block at `number` on the same parent from the attributes that block was built from (same transactions, timestamp, fee recipient, gas limit, EIP-1559 parameters and, post-Jovian, minimum base fee, decoded from the block's extraData), differing in its prevRandao. The build is started by a forkchoice update naming the parent as head with zero safe and finalized hashes, since reth 2.6 refuses a nonzero safe or finalized hash above the head it is given; the method requires the head not to have moved. The payload is returned uninserted. `siblingPayloadAttributes` has unit tests for pre-Holocene, Holocene and Jovian extraData.
- `dsl.ForkchoiceUpdateResult.IsInvalidForkchoiceState()`: requires the engine API's `-38002` error with its `Invalid forkchoice state` message and no payload status.
- `dsl.TestSequencer.SequenceBlocksUntil(t, chainID, attempts, reached)`: builds one block every 2s until a `CheckFunc` passes, retrying failed builds and checks; the L1-advance loop of `sync/elsync/reorg` as a bounded DSL wait.

## Notes on the issue text

- Case 2 asks for an EL sync from scratch "where the first forkchoice update carries safe and finalized hashes reth has not downloaded". op-node never sends such an update to a fresh node on its own: its EL-sync start takes safe and finalized from the empty engine (genesis), and `--syncmode.offset-el-safe` only applies at completion, from blocks already downloaded; kona-node likewise starts from the engine's heads. A consensus client only names undownloaded safe and finalized blocks when its heads are ahead of its engine, so the test produces that state by wiping the datadir under a running consensus client. Under `cl_sync` op-node closes the gap through its peers rather than through EL sync, which is the recovery the matrix cell can have.
- Case 4 asks to pin "that it is not reported as valid". On the bump the answer is `SYNCING`, and because the replaced block is then a sync target the follower downloads it from the sequencer and makes it canonical again; the test pins both, which also separates the bump from `develop`'s `VALID` no-op deterministically.
- The sync-mode dimension does not reach cases 3 and 4: both stop the follower's consensus client before the raw updates, so the cells are `head_already_canonical`/`head_reorgs_to_sibling` and `threshold_7`/`threshold_50`.
- On `develop` the L1-reorg and datadir-wipe scenarios produce no forkchoice rejection at all: op-node's reset paths keep the safe and finalized hashes on the engine's chain (see Findings). The tests still pin the recovery, which the bump's stricter checks must not break.


## CI follow-up

`memory-all-kona-op-reth-fusaka` (CircleCI job 5705185) failed `TestFollowerResyncsFromScratchUnderConsensusClientThatKeptItsHeads/el_sync` under kona-node at the finalized wait (`datadir_wipe_test.go:58`): `operation failed permanently after 210 attempts: expected head for label=finalized to advance to target=59, but got current=0`, 621 s into the cell. The pre-wipe labels (head 183, safe 179, finalized 59), the resync of the unsafe head and the safe head were as expected.

What the follower's kona-node does after the wipe (the CI per-test log carries only its WARN lines; a local run with its INFO lines fills in the rest):

- The first consolidation after the wipe finds no block in the empty engine (``Received `None` block for 186``, `Consolidate(MissingUnsafeL2Block(186))`) and resets. The reset reads the wiped engine's labels (`Loaded current L2 EL forkchoice state unsafe=0 safe=0 finalized=0`) and the sync-start safe search walks back to the finalized block, genesis, so derivation restarts at L1 genesis and the node rebuilds the chain through derivation (`Built and imported new safe block` 1, 2, …: about 185 blocks in 13 s) rather than through EL sync.
- Whenever the derived safe head catches up with the engine's canonical tip while the gossip-fed unsafe head is ahead of it, the next consolidation finds `None` again and resets again; every reset walks back to genesis (`Found suitable L2 safe block l2_safe=0 is_finalized=true is_genesis=true`) and clears the finalization queue (`L2Finalizer::clear` on `Signal::Reset`). Locally the loop ran for the rest of the cell (93 and 94 `MissingUnsafeL2Block` resets in four minutes in the two runs quoted above, every 4 to 8 s in CI), so the finalized label stays at genesis until a finalize task lands between two resets, which locally took 223 s and 282 s.
- In CI the finalize task that landed found the safe head reset below the block it was to finalize (`FinalizeTaskError::BlockNotSafe`), which kona-node treats as `Critical`: at 07:04:01 the follower's kona-node exited with `Failed to start rollup node service: EngineTask(Finalize(BlockNotSafe))`, and nothing advanced for the remaining four minutes of the bound.

Both look like kona-node bugs worth an issue: a reset after an EL datadir wipe restarts derivation at genesis and then loops on `MissingUnsafeL2Block` instead of letting the EL sync, and a finalize request for a block above the reset safe head is fatal instead of being dropped.

The change: #23399's criterion for this scenario is that the sync completes. The cell keeps requiring, under both consensus clients and bounded, that the follower holds the sequencer's unsafe head and is safe at least where it was before the wipe. Being finalized at least where it was before the wipe, which is the consensus client's finalization after its reset rather than the EL's sync, and the consensus-client in-sync check that follows it now run only under op-node; under kona-node the cell skips at that point with a message naming #23399 and quoting the failure (the kona-node defect needs an issue of its own, which the skip should then name instead). The op-node cells run the same sequence as before.

The follower's op-reth is not blameless by inspection alone: in the CI log it answers null by number for block 348 at 07:04:00 while it had received payload 361, and its blocks become canonical in bursts of about six; op-node drives the same EL through the same scenario and passes, so the loop is kona-node's, but whoever takes the issue should know the EL answers null below the highest payload it has received.

Local runs of the committed test (debug op-reth built from this branch, kona-node release binary from `develop`'s `rust/kona`, `-parallel 2`, under `caffeinate`):

```
DEVSTACK_ORCHESTRATOR=sysgo RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_RETH=<debug op-reth> \
  go test -count=1 -timeout 40m -parallel 2 -run TestFollowerResyncsFromScratch -v ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_stale_forkchoice/
--- PASS: TestFollowerResyncsFromScratchUnderConsensusClientThatKeptItsHeads/el_sync (141.66s)
--- PASS: TestFollowerResyncsFromScratchUnderConsensusClientThatKeptItsHeads/cl_sync (148.57s)
ok      github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_stale_forkchoice   149.648s

# the same with DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node RUST_BINARY_PATH_KONA_NODE=<release kona-node>
--- SKIP: TestFollowerResyncsFromScratchUnderConsensusClientThatKeptItsHeads/cl_sync (0.00s)
--- SKIP: TestFollowerResyncsFromScratchUnderConsensusClientThatKeptItsHeads/el_sync (200.31s)
ok      github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_stale_forkchoice   201.370s
```

Under op-node the follower was finalized again about 70 s after the wipe in `el_sync` and at the first poll in `cl_sync`, and its op-node was in sync with the sequencer's at the safe head right after. Under kona-node the `el_sync` cell held the sequencer's unsafe head and was safe where it was 7.5 s after the wipe, then skipped. An earlier pair of runs with the consensus-client check ahead of the finalized wait passed the same way (op-node 141.20 s and 151.73 s; kona-node in sync at the safe head 19 s after the wipe, then skipped).

Stacked on #23438, #23436, #23431, #23427, #23421 and #23418.

Closes #23399

topPRs.title: op-acceptance-tests,op-devstack: cover an op-reth upgrade and rollback over a live datadir
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Every operator upgrades op-reth over a node's live datadir and proofs store, and rolls back when the upgrade misbehaves; nothing tested that path. `op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_upgrade` now runs, for each of {follower, sequencer} x {clean stop, SIGKILL} x {upgrade, rollback}, a node on the previous op-reth release, switches it in place to this tree's op-reth (and back, for the rollback cells), and requires it to resume on the chain its datadir holds, keep up, serve historical proofs that match the sequencer's for the blocks every binary wrote, and log no error. Each cell gets its own system rather than the single four-phase system the issue sketches, so a kill in one cell cannot taint another and a cell can be rerun alone; each phase spans the bump's persistence threshold plus the in-memory buffer, so every binary has both persisted and unpersisted blocks when it is stopped.

The previous release is not built by this repo, so the package skips unless `RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_RETH_PREVIOUS` names it (see docs/ai/acceptance-tests.md). CI skips it until the job provides that binary.

With previous = this branch's base (reth `0fbe428`) and current = the reth 2.6 bump (#23046 head, reth `8d359d01`), under op-node and under kona-node alike: every upgrade cell and both sequencer rollback cells pass. Both follower rollback cells fail: the previous release aborts at startup with `failed to decode notification N from <datadir>/exex/wal/N.wal: wrong msgpack marker FixArray(14)`, because the bump changes the serde shape of the sorted trie updates and hashed storage inside every ExEx notification. A proofs-history node therefore cannot roll back across the bump without first deleting `exex/wal`. Per #23395 that is a release-notes item, not a reason to loosen the test; once it has a tracking issue, the two cells should skip naming it.

The devstack gains the seams the test needs (a per-node binary switch, a recorder of a node's process logs, a skip for binaries no package here builds) and a fix the test exposed: `sysgo.OpReth.Start` waited for the process to announce its RPC endpoints and, when the binary aborted first, blocked until the test deadline (33 minutes per cell here). It now fails as soon as the process exits, naming the node and its exit status.

`go-code-reviewer` was run and every finding was addressed, none dismissed; the general and security reviews were skipped because the change is test infrastructure.

Part of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/23395.

topPRs.title: kona-engine!: keep delegated finalization pending during EL catch-up
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
A kona-node could stop on a finalization target it could not apply yet, in three ways:
- **Delegated catch-up (#23675).** The delegate's finalized block was not downloaded yet, the hash-pinned lookup returned nothing, and the task failed with a Critical error.
- **Reset below a delegated target (#23757, six crashes on a devnet sequencer).** An engine reset lowered the safe head below the delegate's finalized target, which then hit `BlockNotSafe`, also Critical.
- **Reset below a local L1-finality target (#23440's datadir-wipe CI run).** The same `BlockNotSafe` crash, on a by-number target from the node's own `L2Finalizer`.

Now a target above the safe head is skipped with a warning, whatever its source, as op-node's `promoteFinalized` does. A hash-pinned target that is missing from the execution layer is skipped too. Neither sends a forkchoice update. The delegate poll resubmits its target every 4s, the next L1 finality update requests a newer block, and either is finalized once it is safe and present. Making the miss a temporary error instead would hold the task at the head of the engine queue and block the unsafe imports the execution client needs.

Hash pinning (#20877) is kept: a pinned lookup never falls back to the local block at that height, and a returned block whose hash or number differs fails with the new `BlockIdentityMismatch`. A by-number target whose block is missing still fails hard with `BlockNotFound`. Finality never moves above the safe head.

Follows up on #23678.
Closes #23675
Closes #23757
Part of ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#545

**Tests**
- `finalize_target`: rstest table over missing, present, wrong-height, wrong-hash and above-safe targets for both lookup kinds. It asserts the outcome and severity, the exact lookup and forkchoice calls (strict mocks), and the resulting engine state.
- `missing_pinned_target_finalizes_once_engine_has_it`: the first run changes nothing and sends no forkchoice update; the second, once the block exists, finalizes it.
- `missing_pinned_target_does_not_hold_the_queue`: a delegated consolidation answered SYNCING, plus a finalize for a missing pinned block. `drain()` succeeds, the queue empties, and a following unsafe insert runs.
- `finalization_target_survives_resets_below_it` (real `EngineActor`, `by_hash` for #23757 and `by_number` for #23440):
  - A reset restores safe below the target, and the target is skipped without a lookup or FCU. An unsafe import still runs.
  - A second reset repeats the drop.
  - The same target finalizes once the safe head reaches it, and the actor then goes idle with no retry or reset loop.
  - With the guard restricted to hash-pinned targets, the `by_number` case fails with `Finalize(BlockNotSafe)`.
- `DelegateDerivationActor`, which had no tests (scripted delegate, `TestChainProvider`, real queued engine client):
  - It does not poll before engine sync completes.
  - Each poll forwards the safe head, then the hash-pinned finalized head. An unchanged status is resent on every poll, which is the resubmission the skip relies on.
  - A failed fetch, or a non-canonical safe-origin, finalized-origin or `current_l1` hash, forwards nothing and publishes no `current_l1`.

Against develop's `task.rs`, six of the ten engine tests fail; the four that pass cover unchanged behavior. 390 kona-engine and kona-node-service tests pass under nextest, and clippy (`-D warnings`) is clean.

**Interaction with other PRs**
- #23899 (finalized monotonicity) edits the same identity check after the lookup and rewrites `task_test.rs`. Whichever lands second resolves one hunk in `task.rs` and keeps both test sets.
- joshklop's #23846 replaces `DerivationDelegateProvider` with `SyncStatusSource`. If it lands first, the new delegate-actor test fake implements `SyncStatusSource` instead, a change of about five lines.

**Not covered here**
- An end-to-end delegate actor → `EngineActor` test. Its parts are covered separately above.
- A delegated safe target below a gossip-advanced unsafe head while the EL is syncing still resets via `MissingUnsafeL2Block`. That behavior predates this PR.

BREAKING CHANGE: This affects code that uses the `kona-engine` crate and matches `FinalizeTaskError` exhaustively.
- `BlockNotSafe` is removed: a target above the safe head, by hash or by number, is logged and skipped instead of returning a Critical error.
- `BlockIdentityMismatch { actual, expected }` is added. It has Critical severity and is returned when the engine serves a different block for a pinned hash, including a height mismatch that previously returned `BlockNotFound`.

Update match arms accordingly, or use a wildcard.

topPRs.title: op-acceptance-tests: cover proofs history across an unclean shutdown
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
## Why

After a SIGKILL, OOM or power loss, an op-reth proofs-history store usually holds blocks reth's datadir has not persisted (reth persists every `--engine.persistence-threshold` blocks, the store every 5). Nothing reconciles the two at startup, so a node that comes back onto a chain the sequencer rebuilt serves stale `eth_getProof` data and then crash-loops on `ParentHashMismatch` (ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#464, fixed by #23358). Nothing tested the unclean-shutdown path at all; these are the acceptance tests for it.

## What

**`op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs_history_restart`** (sequencer without proofs history as the `eth_getProof` reference, follower with proofs history under the cell's flags, 1s L2 blocks, both op-reths with `--engine.persistence-threshold` and `--engine.memory-block-buffer-target=5` passed explicitly):

- `TestProofsHistoryFollowerRecoversFromUncleanShutdown`: traffic (transfers back and forth plus a contract that writes `NUMBER`/`TIMESTAMP` to two slots) runs until the follower's proofs store has flushed the cell's target block, the follower's op-reth is SIGKILLed at the cell's kill point and its CL stopped. On restart the test reads reth's datadir tip before the CL comes back and requires it below the store's tip (otherwise the cell is not exercising the crash gap), re-peers EL and CL, waits for the follower to be in sync with the sequencer, drives ten more blocks and sweeps `VerifyHistoricalProofsMatch` from the datadir tip to the last traffic block for the message passer, both EOAs and the contract's two slots.
- `TestProofsHistoryFollowerServesRebuiltBlocksAfterUncleanShutdown`: same, but the batcher is stopped up front and the sequencer's op-reth is SIGKILLed right after the follower's, while its own unsafe blocks above the follower's store tip are still in memory; the CLs are stopped once both processes are gone. The restarted sequencer must have its datadir tip below the store tip and at or above the block that completed the workload's funding, and re-sequences the lost heights with different contents (`ReorgTriggered` on the store-tip block); only then is the follower restarted. Skipped naming protocol-team#464, see below.

Matrix, as table-driven subtests: threshold {7, 50} x proofs path {index = `verification-interval=0`, execute = `=1`} x restart sync mode {CL sync, EL sync}. The kill point is paired with the threshold instead of crossing the matrix again: threshold 7 kills mid-buffer (store tip 25, head 27, so the store loses blocks of its own on top of reth's), threshold 50 kills right after the store flushed block 60 (store tip = head, the store's lead over reth is largest). Observed datadir tips at the kill: 21 (once 19 or 20) at threshold 7, 46 at threshold 50, so the store is 4 to 6 and 14 blocks ahead of reth. The sequencer's datadir tip equalled the follower's in every cell.

**`op-devstack`** seams (for #23395, #23396 and later PRs):

- `sysgo.SubProcess.Kill()`: SIGKILL with no interrupt, bounded wait for the exit (`controlledKillWait`), same pipe cleanup as `Stop`. A process that had already died on its own is reaped with a `Sub-process exited before it could be killed` warning rather than reported as killed, so a crash before the kill stays visible. `OpReth.StopUngracefully()` exposes it; `Stop()` stays graceful.
- `stack.UngracefulLifecycle` (`StopUngracefully()`), forwarded by the preset `l2ELFrontend`, and `dsl.L2ELNode.StopUngracefully()` which fails the test for a node that cannot be killed (in-process op-geth).
- `sysgo.MixedSingleChainNodeSpec.L2CLOpts`: per-node op-node options passed to `startL2CLNode` (the mixed runtime passed none before, so every follower ran CL sync). `sysgo.L2CLVerifierSyncMode(mode)` is the option the EL-sync cells use. Ignored for kona-node like `OpRethOpts` is for op-geth.

- `dsl.EOA.DeployBlockRecorder()`: the NUMBER/TIMESTAMP recorder contract both proofs-history packages deploy, moved out of `proofs_history_match` so it is not copied a second time.

Unit tests: `TestSubProcessKillEndsProcessThatIgnoresInterrupts` (a `sh` that traps INT and TERM exits at once, no interrupt is sent, the sub-process restarts afterwards), `TestSubProcessKillOfExitedProcess` (warns instead of claiming a kill, second kill is a no-op), `TestL2CLVerifierSyncMode`.

## Local verification

Debug op-reth built from this branch, `DEVSTACK_ORCHESTRATOR=sysgo RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_RETH=<debug op-reth> go test -count=1 -timeout 40m -parallel 2 -v -run <Test> ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs_history_restart/`:

```
--- PASS: TestProofsHistoryFollowerRecoversFromUncleanShutdown
    threshold_7-index-cl_sync-kill_mid_buffer      (62.01s)   datadir tip 21, store tip 25, head 27; sweep 21..47
    threshold_7-execute-cl_sync-kill_mid_buffer    (57.10s)   21 / 25 / 27; sweep 21..47
    threshold_7-index-el_sync-kill_mid_buffer      (51.78s)   19 / 25 / 27; sweep 19..45
    threshold_7-execute-el_sync-kill_mid_buffer    (51.83s)   21 / 25 / 27; sweep 21..44
    threshold_50-index-cl_sync-kill_after_flush    (92.36s)   46 / 60 / 60; sweep 46..84
    threshold_50-execute-cl_sync-kill_after_flush  (91.73s)   46 / 60 / 60; sweep 46..82
    threshold_50-index-el_sync-kill_after_flush    (92.20s)   46 / 60 / 60; sweep 46..78
    threshold_50-execute-el_sync-kill_after_flush  (87.43s)   46 / 60 / 60; sweep 46..78
ok      op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs_history_restart        329.248s
```

The second test, run once with the skip removed, fails in all eight cells the same way: the sequencer rebuilds the store-tip block with a different hash, the restarted follower imports the chain up to the store's tip, and its op-reth exits on the next block:

```
ERROR Critical task `exex` panicked: `ExEx proofs-history crashed: Parent hash mismatch at block 26: expected 0xac2827d2d59b8cccf35d05720843825354f11528a90d04d6a2c86df9264dd9ab, got 0xfa3ba001f8ce6b5b0ea4af8668481d9501a55f9c4d0da786a78c55249234c2b5`   name=proofs-follower
ERROR shutting down due to error  err="Critical task `exex` panicked: ..."
    Error Trace: op-devstack/dsl/l2_el.go:72 ... proofs_history_restart_test.go:355
    Error:       failed to determine L2BlockRef of latest, could not get payload: read tcp ...: connection reset by peer
